rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Optimization Results sections <U+2013> the authors run their own coupled SWAP simulation-optimization with five CWRF ensemble forecasts for 2002<U+2013>2006 in the Havana Lowlands, Illinois, and report irrigation amounts, yields and profits for several forecast scenarios (Figs. 6<U+2013>9).
rows.notes: The study does report the figures in the passage (Abstract, Conclusions: imperfect reanalysis-based forecasts give about 1<U+2013>3% expected profit gain and 4<U+2013>6% irrigation water reduction relative to a no-rain baseline, up to 5% and 19% in some years). However, the claimed water-saving effect is a pure simulation outcome: the SWAP crop model was calibrated in earlier work (Wang and Cai 2007), and the irrigation/water-saving outputs are never compared with observed irrigation or field measurements in this study. Only the forecast inputs are bias-corrected and skill-tested against observed weather. Under the rule that a model result counts only when its output is checked against measurements of the real system, Q2 is 'no', so Q3<U+2013>Q9 are 'no'. For information: the study does give ensemble-based uncertainty ranges (Figs. 10<U+2013>12), states limitations (reanalysis-driven forecasts are an upper limit, single site, five years, 2004-only Monte Carlo), and notes gains are larger when water is limited; these are not credited because Q2 fails. The passage's mention of 'ETo' is slightly inaccurate <U+2013> the study forecasts rainfall and min/max temperature and uses climatology for humidity, wind and radiation; ET is computed within SWAP. The framework is a modelling tool rather than a farmer-facing app, but it is a forecast-based scheduling decision-support, so not flagged as a technology mismatch.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single-site (Mason County/Havana Lowlands, Illinois, sandy soil, corn, sprinkler irrigation) modelling study; results are scenario comparisons from a simulation-optimization model with no field validation of the water-saving outputs.
